thread:
lena: quick sync 1010 thinking about private/VPC patterns. Two choices we've been kicking around for control-plane + egress in customer VPCs: (A) Regional relay mesh (small relay fleet per region per-customer, routes to our controlplane, and does egress SNAT) vs (B) Per-tenant dedicated endpoints (one lightweight endpoint per tenant with optional customer-owned NAT). Need pros/cons and an initial spike plan.

rahul: high level: mesh = fewer control endpoints to manage but more complex routing for tenant affinity. dedicated endpoints = simpler affinity and IP-preservation but more infra churn and peering entries.

lena: yeah. some specifics: with mesh, we can run a relay pool behind a single peering/transit attachment and route tenant traffic through the pool. That means we only create the VPC peering once per customer region. With dedicated endpoints, we create small ENIs / endpoints per tenant which can explode peering numbers.

ops-sre: operational point: mesh gives us ability to scale egress horizontally and apply centralized filtering/IPS. But blast radius if the relay fleet misconfigs egress ACLs. Need canary configs and automated rollback.

tom: security question: who terminates TLS? If we terminate at relay we can do content-level policing but customer compliance might demand end-to-end TLS passthrough to tenant hosts. Two modes needed: terminate-for-control (mTLS) vs passthrough-for-data (SNI/TCP).

lena: planned: control-plane mTLS terminates at a control proxy (in relay). Model traffic can be passthrough when requested. We support SNI passthrough so tenant backends see original SNI and IP if using dedicated egress. For mesh with SNAT, we can support TPROXY-style hairpin for IP preservation when customer permits.

rahul: TPROXY path detail: requires kernel tweaking and source routing on relay. Not supported on all OS vendors for managed images. If we go that path we must lock the relay OS image and provide a documented support matrix.

infra-eng: cost note 1010 NAT gateways + cross-AZ data transfer are the big drivers. Mesh reduces number of NAT gateways but increases bytes through them. Dedicated endpoints let customers bring their own NAT and avoid our egress charges for very large tenants. We should model costs for 100k, 1M, 10M tokens/day.

ops-sre: reliability: propose active-active relay pairs in-region with route priorities and health checks. Relays should advertise local subnet routes to spokes; spokes try local relay, then remote relay. Add randomized backoff so failover doesn't thunderd.

lena: mapping to product: default = mesh relay with SNAT (low touch), enterprise option = dedicated endpoint + IP preservation + BYO-NAT. Hybrid: tenant can opt into "preserve_source_ip" and we attempt hairpin if supported, otherwise fall back to dedicated egress.

rahul: need configuration API snippet for tenant flags, sample: ```json
{"tenant_id":"acme-123","egress_mode":"mesh","preserve_source_ip":false,"preferred_region":"us-west-2"}
```

ops-sre: +1 spike plan: 1) build relay AMI with both SNAT and TPROXY kernels, 2) deploy mesh for a test tenant, 3) deploy dedicated endpoint for a second tenant, 4) run synthetic traffic (auth handshakes, model streams) and simulate relay failure. Measure handshake p95, model tail latency, and egress $/GB.

tom: also test ACLs and rule propagation timing. We had a previous outage where ACL rollout lagged and new clients got blocked. For mesh we'll need atomic rule application and a rollback plan.

infra-eng: operational metrics to capture: per-tenant connection counts, per-relay network bandwidth, NAT gateway bytes, route propagation time, and TPROXY error rate. Also capture SNI passthrough count vs terminated count.

lena: proposed success criteria for spike: control-plane mTLS handshake p95 < 100ms, model streaming tail p95 within 15% of baseline, egress cost for small tenants within 20% baseline, and failover recovery < 60s for simulated relay crash.

ops-sre: owners: infra-eng for AMI, rahul for relay routing design, tom for security review, lena to coordinate spike. I'll add runbooks and synthetic probes.

deploy-bot: spike-job created: spike-2026-03-05-relay-mesh-vs-dedicated (eu-west-1) :white_check_mark:

rahul: one more thing 1010 cross-account peering. We need a pattern for customers that want controlplane in their account vs us owning a shared account. If controlplane lives in customer account we can minimize peering but must handle onboarding automation (CFN / terraform flow).

lena: agree. onboarding automation and IAM least-priv are blockers for customer-owned controlplane. We'll add those as acceptance criteria for the enterprise path.

ops-sre: OK. I'll schedule a 2-week spike starting Monday and we'll capture metrics + a short writeup. If results are promising we draft an RFC with diagrams and runbook playbooks.
